emergency.title: Get emergency care now if any of these are true
items: The pain is so bad you cannot sit still, or you cannot find a position that eases it.
The pain is severe and does not let up.
You keep vomiting, or you cannot keep water down.
You have a fever or chills.
Breathing is hard, or your heart is racing.
You feel faint, very dizzy, confused, or too weak to sip water.
Your skin or the whites of your eyes look yellow.
You vomit blood, or the vomit looks like coffee grounds.
Your stool is black, maroon, or bloody.
You have chest pain or pressure.

flareSteps.title: Sit up
flareSteps.text: Lean on pillows. Keep your knees a little bent. Lying flat can make this pain worse. Loosen anything tight around your waist. If a position hurts more, leave it.

flareSteps.title: Tiny sips only
flareSteps.text: If you are vomiting, do not force food or drink. If drinks stay down, take small sips of water. Do not start a long fast unless your own clinician already told you to pause food.

flareSteps.title: Only your plan
flareSteps.text: Take only the medicine your own clinician already told you to take, at the time they told you. Harbor will not give you a drug name or a dose. If you have no plan and the pain is severe, get care. Do not guess.

callToday: The pain is worse than your usual pattern, but you are still able to sit and sip.
You are losing weight without trying.
Stools are oily, pale, or very hard to flush, or diarrhea is new.
You are much more thirsty, much more hungry, or passing urine more often.
The treatment you already have is not helping.
You cannot eat enough to hold your weight.
A new symptom is scaring you.
steadyRules: No alcohol. Not beer, not wine, not a small drink.
Smaller meals, more often. A large plate makes the pancreas work harder.
Keep a drink nearby. Dehydration can set off a flare.
Choose lean food. Skip fried food and cream sauces.
If enzymes were prescribed, take them with the meal, the way you were shown.
If a red-flag sign shows up, stop following recipes and get care.

guides.title: When to get help now
body: Mayo Clinic says to get immediate help if the pain is so severe you cannot sit still or cannot find a position that is more comfortable.
Cleveland Clinic says to go to the emergency department for severe, constant belly pain, especially with repeated vomiting, fever, trouble breathing, fainting, severe dizziness, or a fast heartbeat.
The National Pancreas Foundation also says to get immediate care for yellow skin or eyes, fever or chills, trouble breathing, or signs of dehydration.
Vomiting blood, vomit that looks like coffee grounds, and black or bloody stool are emergency signs. Do not wait those out at home.

guides.title: Call your own clinician today
body: You do not have to be in the emergency list to need a call. Call the same day if the pain is climbing past your usual, food will not stay down, or you are losing weight.
Oily, pale, very smelly stools can mean food is not being absorbed. New strong thirst, hunger, or urination can be a sign of diabetes. Both need your clinician, not a new diet from an app.
Cleveland Clinic says to call if symptoms are getting worse, you are losing weight, or your current treatment is not helping.

guides.title: What this pain often does
body: Pain is often in the upper belly. It can spread to the back. It often gets worse after eating. It can be there for hours, or it can be a constant ache.
Cleveland Clinic says it can feel worse when you lie flat, cough, exercise, or eat a heavier meal.
Some people with chronic pancreatitis have little or no pain. You are not doing this wrong if your days do not match someone else's.

guides.title: What actually helps pain
body: Mayo Clinic says there is no specific medicine to treat pancreatitis. In a bad attack, teams often use pain medicine, fluids, and a careful return to food. That is hospital care when the attack is severe.

For ongoing pain, a clinician may look for a fixable cause, such as a blocked duct or stones. Some people see a pain specialist. Some are offered a nerve block, a stent, or surgery. Those are medical decisions.
Harbor cannot turn the pain off. It can help you sit up, sip safely, follow the plan you were already given, and know when to get help.

guides.title: A position that is often easier
body: Try sitting up, pillows behind you, knees a little bent. Lying flat can make the pain worse.
Loosen a tight waistband. Stay as still as you need to. Skip exercise during a flare.
If the new position hurts more, stop it. If no position is bearable, that is a reason to get emergency care.

guides.title: Food when the flare is bad
body: The National Pancreas Foundation says a doctor may tell you to limit food, sometimes for a day or two, during a flare. Only do that if your own clinician has told you to. Do not invent a long fast. A hospital fast, with a drip or a feeding tube, is not something to copy at home.

When pain is severe and you are allowed to drink, clear liquids are the usual first step: apple juice, cranberry juice, white grape juice, gelatin, and broth. They are not a full diet. Move back to food as soon as you can, on the schedule you were given.
MedlinePlus discharge advice for after an episode starts with broth or gelatin, then bland foods: rice, dry toast, crackers, bananas, and applesauce.
If you are vomiting, do not force any of this. Not keeping water down is a reason to get care.

guides.title: Food on steadier days
body: Mayo Clinic describes a balanced plate: vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and lean protein, without high-fat foods. NIDDK describes a low-fat plan, small frequent meals, plenty of fluids, limited caffeine, and no alcohol.
The National Pancreas Foundation says several small meals are often easier than three large ones, and that dehydration can trigger a flare.

A European nutrition guideline, ESPEN, says people with chronic pancreatitis usually should not stay on a very strict low-fat diet forever, because the body still needs energy. If you are underweight, the need is more protein and more calories, in five or six smaller meals.

Both sides agree on the part that matters today: no alcohol, no greasy meals, smaller portions, and a dietitian if weight is falling. Harbor's flare list is the gentler end on purpose. It is not a reason to under-eat all month.

guides.title: About fat, said plainly
body: One Cleveland Clinic article suggests keeping fat under about 30 grams a day and mentions MCT oil as something a dietitian may add. Do not start MCT oil during a flare, and do not start it on your own.
ESPEN's guideline says a balanced diet is preferred once chronic pancreatitis is established. A very low-fat plan can make weight loss worse.
Let your dietitian set your fat target. Until then, skip fried food and cream, and use the flare list when you are sore.

guides.title: Enzyme pills
body: If diarrhea or weight loss is from the pancreas not making enough enzymes, a clinician may prescribe enzyme pills with meals. Mayo Clinic says they help the body break down food. They are not a promise to erase pain.
The dose is individual. Do not change it from this app. Take them the way the prescriber showed you, with food, not on an empty stomach.
A hot drink is a poor way to swallow them. If capsules are hard to swallow, ask before you open them. Do not stop them just because you had a better week.
NIDDK also says a clinician may check vitamins A, D, E, and K, and sometimes B12, if food is not being absorbed. Ask before you start a vitamin on your own.

guides.title: Alcohol and smoking
body: Do not drink alcohol. Mayo Clinic, NIDDK, Cleveland Clinic, and the National Pancreas Foundation all say to stop, even when alcohol was not the original cause. It can bring the inflammation back.
If stopping is hard, ask your clinician for help. That is a medical request, not a character test.
Smoking makes pancreatic disease worse and raises the risk of pancreatic cancer. Ask for help to quit. You do not have to do it by willpower alone.

guides.title: Water
body: Pancreatitis can dry you out, and dehydration can set off another flare. Keep a drink you can see.
On a sore day, small sips beat a large glass you throw up. If water will not stay down, get care.
NIDDK says to limit caffeine. On a flare day, choose water or broth before coffee.

guides.title: Weight, stools, and blood sugar
body: Losing weight without trying, and stools that are oily or very smelly, belong on a call list. Do not answer that by eating a large fatty meal.
Chronic pancreatitis can damage the cells that make insulin. New thirst, hunger, or frequent urination needs a check.
Your team may add a dietitian. That referral is worth asking for.

guides.title: Medicines
body: Some medicines can inflame the pancreas. Do not stop a prescription because a website says it might. Ask your clinician before you change any medicine.
Do not pick a pain pill from this app. Not a name, and not a dose. Use only the written plan you were given. If that plan is not holding a severe flare, the next step is care, not a bigger guess.
Bring your flare notes to the visit. A pain specialist is a reasonable thing to ask about when pain is running your days.

guides.title: Questions worth asking
body: What should I do in the first hour of a flare?
Which pain medicines are mine, and which should I avoid?
Do I need enzyme pills? When do I take them?
Should I see a dietitian, and what fat target is right for me?
Do I need checks for vitamins, diabetes, or my weight?
Is this pain something a specialist should look at, such as a duct, stones, or a nerve block?
What change in weight or stool should make me call you the same day?

sources.name: NIDDK

staples.name: Clear apple juice or white grape juice

foods.name: Ice chips
foods.fat: None
foods.line: Let a chip melt. Do not chew a mouthful of ice.
steps: Start with one or two chips.
Let them melt in your mouth.
Wait a few minutes before more.
If you vomit, stop and get medical care.
foods.note: Only if your clinician has not told you to take nothing by mouth.

foods.name: Small sips of water
foods.fat: None
foods.line: The first drink to try when a sip will stay down.
steps: Sit up.
Take one small sip.
Wait. If it stays down, take another.
If water will not stay down, stop and get care. Do not force a full glass.
foods.note: Dehydration can set off a flare, but vomiting changes the plan. Care comes before a quota.

foods.name: Oral rehydration drink
foods.fat: Check the label
foods.line: A pharmacy drink made for dehydration. Not a sports soda binge.
needs: An oral rehydration drink from a pharmacy
steps: Choose a drink made for rehydration, not an energy drink.
Sip it cold or cool. Do not chug it.
Follow the label, and your clinician if they gave you a limit.
Stop if you feel sick.
foods.note: If you have diabetes, kidney disease, or a sodium limit, ask which product is yours before you rely on one.

foods.name: Fat-free chicken broth
foods.fat: Usually under 1 gram if the carton says fat-free
foods.line: Warm the carton. Do not boil it. Skip creamy soup.
steps: Check the carton. It should say fat-free, not creamy.
Warm one cup until it is pleasant to sip. Do not boil it.
Sit up. Sip slowly.
If a fat layer is floating, chill the mug and lift the fat off, or start over with a fat-free carton.
foods.note: Choose low-sodium if your clinician limited salt. The National Pancreas Foundation lists broth as a clear liquid for a severe day.

foods.name: Fat-free vegetable broth
foods.fat: Usually under 1 gram if it is fat-free
foods.line: The same idea as chicken broth, if you do not eat meat.
steps: Read the label. Skip cartons with cream, coconut milk, or oil high on the list.
Warm one cup. Do not boil it.
Sip it slowly, sitting up.
Stop if nausea rises.
foods.note: Low-sodium if salt is limited for you.

foods.name: Fat-free beef broth
foods.fat: Only if the label says fat-free
foods.line: Use it only when the label says fat-free. Many beef broths are not.
steps: Read the fat line on the label before you open it.
If it is not fat-free, do not use it today.
Warm one cup and sip it slowly.
Stop if it feels heavy.

foods.name: Apple juice
foods.fat: None
foods.line: Half juice, half water. Sip slowly.
steps: Pour half a cup of apple juice.
Add half a cup of water.
Sit up. Take a small sip. Wait before the next one.
Stop if you feel sick. If you vomit, get medical care.
foods.note: If you have diabetes, juice can raise your blood sugar. Keep it small and follow your diabetes plan.

foods.name: White grape juice
foods.fat: None
foods.line: Half juice, half water. Sip slowly.
steps: Pour half a cup of white grape juice.
Add half a cup of water.
Sit up. Take a small sip. Wait before the next one.
Stop if you feel sick. If you vomit, get medical care.
foods.note: If you have diabetes, juice can raise your blood sugar. Keep it small and follow your diabetes plan.

foods.name: Cranberry juice
foods.fat: None
foods.line: Half juice, half water. Sip slowly.
steps: Pour half a cup of cranberry juice.
Add half a cup of water.
Sit up. Take a small sip. Wait before the next one.
Stop if you feel sick. If you vomit, get medical care.
foods.note: If you take warfarin, a blood thinner, ask before cranberry. If you have diabetes, keep the cup small.

foods.name: Plain gelatin
foods.fat: Usually none
foods.line: A ready cup, or a box made with water. No whipped topping.
needs: One plain gelatin cup, or a box made as the box says
steps: Choose a plain gelatin. Skip anything with cream or fruit in heavy syrup.
If you make a box, follow the box and use water.
Eat it cool, a small cup.
This is not a full meal. Go back to other food as soon as you can.
foods.note: Gelatin is on the National Pancreas Foundation clear-liquid list. It will not treat the pain.

foods.name: Diluted juice ice pop
foods.fat: None, if you made it from diluted juice
foods.line: A pop you froze earlier from half juice, half water. Not a cream bar.
needs: An ice pop made from diluted apple or white grape juice
steps: Only use a pop you made from juice and water, or a label that shows no fat and no cream.
Eat it slowly, sitting up.
One is enough to start.
Skip store bars with coconut, cream, or chocolate.
foods.note: Make a few on a steady day and keep them in the freezer. If you have diabetes, count the juice.

foods.name: Weak decaf tea
foods.fat: None if you add no milk
foods.line: A short steep. No milk. No sugar required.
steps: Steep the bag for a short time, then take it out.
Add no milk, cream, or honey at this stage.
Let it cool until it is warm, not scorching.
Sip slowly. Coffee can wait.
foods.note: NIDDK says to limit caffeine. Decaf is the flare-day choice. Skip tea if your clinician told you to stay on clear liquids only and did not include it.

foods.name: Unsweetened applesauce
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: The jar is enough. No sugar stirred in.
steps: Open a jar or a cup that says unsweetened.
Eat a small cup, cool or room temperature.
Do not add butter, sugar, or granola.
Stop if your stomach turns.
foods.note: MedlinePlus lists applesauce among the bland foods after an episode.

foods.name: Ripe banana
foods.fat: Under 1 gram in one half
foods.line: Yellow, with a few brown spots. Easy to chew.
steps: Peel half of a ripe banana.
Eat it slowly.
Save the other half.
Stop if it sits like a stone.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium, ask before bananas, melon, or potatoes.

foods.name: Saltine crackers
foods.fat: About 1 gram in four plain saltines. Read the box.
foods.line: Plain saltines. Not butter crackers.
steps: Take two to four plain saltines.
Eat them dry, or with a sip of broth.
Do not add cheese or peanut butter today.
Stop at a small handful.
foods.note: They are salty. If salt is limited for you, keep the count small.

foods.name: Plain rice cakes
foods.fat: Usually under 1 gram if they are plain
foods.line: Plain, not caramel, not chocolate, not with seeds.
steps: Choose a plain rice cake. Read the fat line.
Eat one slowly with a sip of water or broth.
A second is fine if the first sits well.
Skip flavored cakes with icing or chocolate.

foods.name: Melba toast
foods.fat: Low if the box says so. Read it.
foods.line: Dry toast you do not have to make.
steps: Take a few plain pieces.
Eat them dry.
Sip water or broth with them if your mouth is dry.
Stop if they scratch or hurt to swallow. Switch to applesauce or gelatin.

foods.name: Canned pears in juice
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: In juice, drained. Not in heavy syrup.
steps: Read the can. It should say juice, not heavy syrup.
Drain it.
Eat a small cup.
If you have diabetes, count it in your fruit plan.

foods.name: Canned peaches in juice
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: In juice, drained. The same rule as pears.
steps: Check the label for juice, not syrup.
Drain the cup.
Eat it slowly.
Skip peach pie filling.
foods.note: If you have diabetes, count this in your fruit plan.

foods.name: Leftover plain rice
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if it was cooked with no oil
foods.line: Rice you already made. Warm it with a splash of water.
steps: Only use rice that was cooked without oil or butter.
Warm it with a splash of water, covered, so it steams soft.
Eat half a cup, sitting up.
If it was fried rice, do not eat it today.
foods.note: This is the 2 a.m. option. No cooking from scratch.

foods.name: Dry toast
foods.fat: About 1 gram in a plain slice. Read the bread bag.
foods.line: One slice. No butter. White bread is often easier today than seeded bread.
steps: Toast one slice until it is dry, not dark.
Eat it with no butter, oil, or avocado.
A scrape of jelly is optional sugar, not fat. Skip jelly if you are limiting sugar.
One slice first. Wait before a second.
foods.note: MedlinePlus lists dry toast as a bland food after an episode. You do not have to stay on white bread forever.

foods.name: Plain bagel, no spread
foods.fat: Low on a plain bagel. Cream cheese is not low.
foods.line: Half of a plain bagel. Nothing spread on it.
steps: Toast half of a plain bagel if you want it warm.
Do not add cream cheese, butter, or peanut butter.
Eat it slowly.
Stop at half.

foods.name: English muffin, dry
foods.fat: About 1 gram in one plain half
foods.line: One half, toasted, with nothing on it.
needs: Half of a plain English muffin
steps: Toast one half.
Eat it dry.
Skip butter and cheese.
Wait before the other half.

foods.name: Plain pretzels
foods.fat: Varies. Read the label. Skip buttery pretzels.
foods.line: A small handful of plain pretzels, not a bag.
steps: Check the label. Choose plain, not chocolate or yogurt-coated.
Put a small handful in a bowl. Do not eat from the bag.
Chew well. Sip water.
Stop when the bowl is empty.
foods.note: Salty. Keep it small if salt is limited for you.

foods.name: Baked peeled apple
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: Peel it. Soften it with water. No sugar crust.
steps: Peel the apple and cut it into slices.
Put it in a dish with a spoon of water. Cover it.
Microwave or bake until it is soft.
Eat half. Add no butter.
foods.note: Peel and cook it. A raw apple is harder work on a flare day.

foods.name: Soft white rice
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: Rice and water and a pinch of salt. That is the whole dish.
steps: Rinse the rice if you like.
Simmer it in the water until it is soft, not firm.
Add no butter, no oil, and no soy sauce today.
Eat half a cup. Keep the rest for later.
foods.note: White rice is gentler during a flare than a heavy brown-rice bowl. Brown rice can come back on a steady week.

foods.name: Rice porridge
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: Rice cooked with extra water until it is a soft spoon food.
steps: Put the rice and water in a small pot.
Simmer until the rice falls apart and looks like a soft porridge. Stir now and then.
Add a pinch of salt. Add no oil.
Eat a small bowl warm, not scorching.
foods.note: This is the same idea as congee. It is often easier than a plate of separate foods.

foods.name: Cream of Rice, with water
foods.fat: Under 1 gram when made with water
foods.line: The cereal name says cream. Use water anyway.
steps: Follow the box, but use water, not milk.
Cook until smooth.
Add no butter.
Eat a small bowl.

foods.name: Cream of Wheat, with water
foods.fat: Under 1 gram when made with water
foods.line: Another soft cereal. Water, not milk, on a flare day.
steps: Cook it with water, as the box shows for a thin cereal.
Skip milk, butter, and brown sugar today.
Let it cool until you can eat it comfortably.
Start with a small bowl.

foods.name: Grits with water
foods.fat: Under 1 gram when made with water
foods.line: Soft grits. No cheese. No butter.
steps: Stir plain grits into simmering water so they do not clump.
Cook until soft.
Salt lightly. Add no cheese, bacon, or butter.
Eat a small bowl.
foods.note: Choose plain grits, not a cheese packet.

foods.name: Oatmeal with water
foods.fat: About 2 grams in a third cup of dry oats, before toppings
foods.line: A smaller, softer bowl than a loaded breakfast.
steps: Cook the oats in water until soft.
Add no milk, nuts, or peanut butter.
A few bites of banana on top are fine if fruit is sitting well.
If oats make you bloat, skip them today and use rice or cream of rice.
foods.note: Oats have a little more fat and fiber than white rice. Wait for them if you are still at the sip stage.

foods.name: Plain pasta
foods.fat: About 1 gram in half a cup of plain cooked pasta
foods.line: Soft noodles. No oil, no cheese, no jar sauce.
needs: A small handful of plain pasta
steps: Boil a small amount of pasta until it is soft.
Drain it. Do not toss it in oil.
If you want moisture, add a spoon of fat-free broth.
Eat half a cup.

foods.name: Plain egg noodles
foods.fat: A little higher than plain pasta. Read the bag. Keep the bowl small.
foods.line: Soft egg noodles with broth, not a butter sauce.
needs: A small nest of plain egg noodles
steps: Boil the noodles until soft.
Drain them.
Moisten with fat-free broth. Add no butter.
Eat half a cup. Skip this if eggs bother you.

foods.name: Rice noodles in broth
foods.fat: Low if the noodles are plain and the broth is fat-free
foods.line: Soft rice noodles in fat-free broth.
needs: A small handful of rice noodles
steps: Heat the broth.
Soften the noodles in it until they are tender.
Add no oil and no coconut milk.
Eat the noodles and sip some of the broth. Leave it if your stomach says the bowl is enough.

foods.name: Plain couscous
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you stir it with water, not oil
foods.line: Pour hot water over it. Cover it. Fluff it. No oil.
steps: Put the couscous in a bowl.
Pour on the hot water the box asks for. Cover it.
Wait about 5 minutes. Fluff it with a fork. Add no oil.
Eat half a cup.
foods.note: This is wheat. Skip it if you do not eat gluten, and use rice instead.

foods.name: Boiled potato
foods.fat: Almost none, with no butter
foods.line: Boiled until soft. Peel if the skin bothers you.
steps: Peel the potato if skins bother you. Cut it into chunks.
Boil until a fork goes in easily.
Drain it. Add a pinch of salt. Add no butter or sour cream.
Eat half. Keep the rest plain in the fridge.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium, ask first.

foods.name: Microwave potato
foods.fat: Almost none, with no butter
foods.line: The flare-day potato when you cannot stand at the stove.
steps: Wash it. Poke it with a fork a few times.
Microwave until soft, about 5 to 8 minutes, turning once.
Let it cool a little. Split it.
Eat half with no butter. A spoon of fat-free broth can moisten it.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium, ask first.

foods.name: Mashed potato with broth
foods.fat: Low only if you mash with broth, not butter or cream
foods.line: Soft potatoes mashed with fat-free broth.
steps: Boil or microwave a potato until soft.
Mash it with a splash of fat-free broth.
Do not add butter, milk, cheese, or gravy.
Eat half a cup.

foods.name: Plain sweet potato
foods.fat: Almost none, with no butter
foods.line: Microwave it. Cinnamon is fine. Marshmallows are not.
steps: Poke the sweet potato. Microwave until soft.
Split it and let it cool a little.
Eat half, plain, or with a shake of cinnamon.
Add no butter and no sugar glaze.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium, ask first.

foods.name: Plain canned pumpkin
foods.fat: Under 1 gram for plain pumpkin
foods.line: The can must say pumpkin, not pumpkin pie mix.
steps: Read the can. Pie mix is a different food. Do not use it.
Warm half a cup with a spoon of water.
Add cinnamon if you want. Add no cream.
Eat it like a soft side.

foods.name: Steamed carrots
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you add no oil
foods.line: Cooked until soft. No glaze, no honey butter.
steps: Wash it. Cut it into small pieces if you need to.
Steam it, boil it, or microwave it with a spoon of water until soft.
Add no oil, butter, or sauce.
Eat a small cup. Stop if your belly feels tight.

foods.name: Green beans
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you add no oil
foods.line: Frozen or fresh, cooked soft, no sauce packet.
steps: Wash it. Cut it into small pieces if you need to.
Steam it, boil it, or microwave it with a spoon of water until soft.
Add no oil, butter, or sauce.
Eat a small cup. Stop if your belly feels tight.

foods.name: Steamed zucchini
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you add no oil
foods.line: Soft cubes. No oil. Skip the seeds if they bother you.
steps: Wash it. Cut it into small pieces if you need to.
Steam it, boil it, or microwave it with a spoon of water until soft.
Add no oil, butter, or sauce.
Eat a small cup. Stop if your belly feels tight.

foods.name: Cooked spinach
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you add no oil
foods.line: Wilted in a spoon of water. No garlic oil.
steps: Wash it. Cut it into small pieces if you need to.
Steam it, boil it, or microwave it with a spoon of water until soft.
Add no oil, butter, or sauce.
Eat a small cup. Stop if your belly feels tight.

foods.name: Winter squash
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if you add no oil
foods.line: Soft cubes of butternut or acorn. No brown sugar.
steps: Wash it. Cut it into small pieces if you need to.
Steam it, boil it, or microwave it with a spoon of water until soft.
Add no oil, butter, or sauce.
Eat a small cup. Stop if your belly feels tight.

foods.name: Noodles in fat-free broth
foods.fat: Low when both parts are plain
foods.line: A bowl of soft noodles and broth. Not a creamy soup.
needs: A small handful of plain pasta or rice noodles
steps: Heat the broth.
Cook the noodles in it until soft.
Add no cream, no cheese, and no oily drizzle.
Eat a small bowl, sitting up.

foods.name: Nonfat yogurt
foods.fat: 0 grams only if the cup says nonfat. Low-fat is a later-day food.
foods.line: Plain nonfat yogurt. No granola on top.
steps: Check the cup. It should say nonfat or 0% fat.
Eat it plain, or with a few bites of banana or drained pears.
Skip granola, nuts, honey clusters, and full-fat yogurt today.
If dairy bothers you, skip this and use applesauce.

foods.name: Nonfat cottage cheese
foods.fat: Low only in the nonfat tub. Read it.
foods.line: A small scoop of nonfat cottage cheese. Nothing fried on the side.
steps: Read the tub. Choose nonfat.
Serve half a cup.
Eat it alone or with canned pears in juice.
Skip it if dairy bothers you.
foods.note: It is salty. Keep the scoop small if salt is limited.

foods.name: Tuna in water
foods.fat: About 1 gram in half a can packed in water. Oil-packed is a different food.
foods.line: Drain a can packed in water. No mayonnaise.
steps: Read the can. It must say water, not oil.
Drain it well.
Eat half, plain or with lemon, next to rice or rice cakes.
Save the rest in the fridge and finish it the same day.
foods.note: Skip if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Sliced turkey breast
foods.fat: Low in plain turkey breast. Not low in salami or bologna.
foods.line: A few slices of plain turkey breast. No mayo.
steps: Choose turkey breast, not a smoked fatty cold cut.
Eat two or three slices, rolled or with a rice cake.
Add no mayonnaise and no cheese.
It is salty. Stop at a few slices.

foods.name: Dry egg-white scramble
foods.fat: Almost none if the pan is truly dry
foods.line: Whites only. A nonstick pan. No oil if you can turn them.
steps: Separate two whites. Save or discard the yolks. The fat is in the yolk.
Pour the whites into a nonstick pan over low heat.
Stir until just set. Add no cheese and no butter.
Eat them with toast or rice. Skip eggs entirely if they bother you.
foods.note: If the pan will stick and burn, a half-second spray is the most fat to add. Do not pour in oil.

foods.name: Egg-white drop soup
foods.fat: Very low
foods.line: Fat-free broth with a ribbon of egg white. Not a greasy restaurant bowl.
steps: Heat the broth until it simmers.
Stir the broth, and slowly pour in the egg white.
Cook for a minute until the white sets.
Eat a small bowl. Skip this if eggs bother you.

foods.name: Poached chicken breast
foods.fat: About 2 grams in 2 ounces of skinless white meat, with no oil
foods.line: Simmered in water. No skin. No frying.
steps: Put the breast in a small pot and cover it with water.
Simmer gently until the center is cooked through. Do not boil it dry.
Slice it thin.
Eat a few slices with rice. Refrigerate the rest for the next small meal.
foods.note: Cook poultry through. If standing at the stove is too much, skip to sliced turkey from the fridge.

foods.name: Baked chicken breast
foods.fat: About 2 grams in 2 ounces, skinless, no oil
foods.line: Oven, no skin, no breading.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Put the breast in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Bake until the center is cooked through.
Slice it and eat a small serving. No gravy.

foods.name: Baked cod
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the cod in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Baked haddock
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the haddock in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Baked pollock
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the pollock in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Baked tilapia
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the tilapia in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Baked sole
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the sole in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Baked flounder
foods.fat: About 1 gram if you use no oil
foods.line: No breading. No butter. Lemon is enough.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F, or set up a steamer.
Put the flounder in a dish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Cook until it flakes, about 10 to 15 minutes. Do not fry it.
Eat a few bites with rice or potato. Stop if the pain rises.
foods.note: Skip this if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Steamed shrimp
foods.fat: Under 1 gram in a few plain shrimp
foods.line: Steamed or boiled. No butter. No cocktail sauce today.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a simmer, or set a steamer.
Cook the shrimp just until they turn pink and firm.
Eat a few with lemon. Add no butter and no creamy sauce.
Skip this entirely if you have a shellfish allergy.

foods.name: Crab in broth
foods.fat: Low when the crab is plain and the broth is fat-free
foods.line: Plain crab meat warmed in fat-free broth.
needs: A small amount of plain crab meat
steps: Check that the crab has no creamy dressing.
Warm it in fat-free broth.
Eat a small cup.
Skip this if you have a shellfish allergy.
foods.note: Avoid imitation crab if the label shows added fat you do not want today.

foods.name: Silken tofu in broth
foods.fat: About 2 to 4 grams in a small soft serving. Read the box.
foods.line: Soft cubes in hot fat-free broth.
needs: A small block of silken tofu
steps: Open silken tofu and cut a few cubes.
Warm them in fat-free broth. Do not fry them.
Eat the cubes and sip a little broth.
Skip this if soy bothers you.
foods.note: Firm tofu cooked in oil is a different dish. Not today.

foods.name: Chicken and rice soup
foods.fat: Low if you use breast meat, fat-free broth, and no oil
foods.line: Breast meat, rice, and broth. Skim any fat you see.
needs: A few slices of skinless chicken breast
steps: Heat fat-free broth.
Add cooked rice and a little chicken breast.
If any fat rises, spoon it off.
Eat a small bowl. Chew the meat well.
foods.note: Use chicken you already cooked plainly, or a few slices of the breast from today. Do not use a creamy canned soup.

foods.name: Turkey and rice soup
foods.fat: Low with breast meat and fat-free broth
foods.line: The same bowl as the chicken soup, made with turkey breast.
steps: Heat the broth.
Add rice and a little turkey breast.
Skim any fat.
Eat a small bowl.
foods.note: Do not use sausage, skin, or pan drippings.

foods.name: Watermelon
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: A small bowl once sips are staying down. A huge wedge is too much volume.
steps: Cut a small bowl of cubes.
Eat them slowly.
Do not eat a half melon.
Skip it if you are still vomiting or still on liquids only.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium or sugar, ask first. This belongs in the calming stage, not the worst hour.

foods.name: Cantaloupe
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: Ripe, soft, a small bowl.
steps: Cut a small bowl.
Eat it slowly.
Skip the prosciutto and cheese plate it sometimes comes with.
Wait for this until liquids are staying down.
foods.note: If your clinician limited potassium, ask first.

foods.name: Honeydew
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: A small bowl of ripe honeydew.
steps: Cut a small bowl.
Eat it slowly, sitting up.
Stop if it feels like too much water in your stomach.
Not for the worst hour, when even sips are hard.

foods.name: A few strawberries
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: A few, not a pint. Hull them. No cream.
steps: Wash two or three berries.
Hull them. Cut them if the seeds bother you.
Eat them with no cream and no sugar crust.
If seeds bother you, choose applesauce instead.
foods.note: This is a calming-stage fruit. Skip it while you are still on clear liquids.

foods.name: A few blueberries
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: A small handful. Not a smoothie with seeds and yogurt drinks.
steps: Rinse a small handful.
Eat them one at a time, or stir them into water-oatmeal.
Do not blend them into a fat-containing smoothie today.
Stop if the skins bother you.

foods.name: Ripe papaya
foods.fat: Under 1 gram in a small cup
foods.line: Ripe, soft, seeded. It is fruit. It is not a treatment.
steps: Cut a small cup of ripe orange flesh. Discard the seeds.
Eat it plain.
Do not take a papaya pill in its place.
Stop if your mouth or belly feels irritated.
foods.note: Papaya is only food here. It does not replace enzymes your clinician prescribed.

foods.name: Banana and rice
foods.portion: Half a banana and half a cup of rice
foods.fat: Under 1 gram if the rice was plain
foods.line: Two foods that often sit well, on one small plate.
needs: Half a cup of plain rice
steps: Warm leftover plain rice with a splash of water, or use rice you just made.
Put half a cup on a plate with half a banana.
Eat the rice and banana separately if mixing them sounds unpleasant.
Stop when the plate is done. Do not refill it yet.
foods.note: Use this when sips have been staying down and you are ready for soft food.

foods.name: Toast and applesauce
foods.portion: One slice and a small cup
foods.fat: About 1 gram, mostly from the bread
foods.line: The bland pair from discharge sheets, put on one plate.
needs: A small cup of unsweetened applesauce
steps: Toast one slice. Leave it dry.
Put a small cup of unsweetened applesauce beside it.
Alternate bites. Sit up.
Wait before you make more.

foods.name: White fish and potato
foods.fat: Low if both are cooked with no oil
foods.line: A little baked white fish and a plain potato.
needs: A small cod, haddock, pollock, tilapia, sole, or flounder fillet
steps: Cook the potato in the microwave or boil it.
Bake or steam the fish with a spoon of water. Do not bread it.
Put a few bites of each on a plate. Add lemon if you want.
Eat slowly. Refrigerate the rest for another small meal.
foods.note: Skip if you have a fish allergy.

foods.name: Chicken and rice, a few bites
foods.fat: Low if both were cooked with no oil
foods.line: Use food you already cooked. This is assembly, not a project.
needs: A few slices of plain chicken breast
Half a cup of plain rice
steps: Warm the rice with a splash of water.
Add a few slices of skinless chicken cooked without frying.
Eat sitting up.
Stop at this small plate even if you want the rest an hour later.
foods.note: If enzymes were prescribed, take them with these bites, the way you were shown.

foods.name: Potato and carrots
foods.fat: Under 1 gram
foods.line: Two soft vegetables. A full plate of plants, still plain.
steps: Cut both small.
Boil or steam them until a fork slides in.
Add a pinch of salt. Add no butter.
Eat a small bowl.

foods.name: Yogurt and pears
foods.fat: Low only if the yogurt is nonfat and the pears are drained
foods.line: Nonfat yogurt with drained pears in juice.
steps: Drain a few pear slices.
Put them on a small cup of nonfat yogurt.
Add no granola.
Skip this if dairy bothers you.

foods.name: Turkey and soft noodles
foods.fat: Low with breast meat and no oil
foods.line: Soft noodles, fat-free broth, a little turkey breast.
steps: Cook a small amount of noodles in fat-free broth.
Add turkey breast, not sausage.
Skim any fat.
Eat a small bowl.

foods.name: Alcohol
foods.line: No beer, wine, or liquor. Not a sip to settle your stomach.
foods.note: Mayo Clinic, NIDDK, Cleveland Clinic, and the National Pancreas Foundation all say to stop.

foods.name: Fried food
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Fries, fried chicken, donuts, anything cooked in a pan of oil.
foods.note: Fat makes a sore pancreas work harder. This is the first category to leave.

foods.name: Cream and butter
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Cream soups, Alfredo, ice cream, butter, mayonnaise, and creamy dressing.
foods.find: cream butter mayo ice cream alfredo

foods.name: Cheese and whole milk
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Cheese plates, whole milk, and whipped cream. Nonfat yogurt is the dairy exception on this list.

foods.name: Fatty meat
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Bacon, sausage, ribs, skin-on poultry, and fatty beef.
foods.note: Lean breast meat is on the eat list. These are not that.

foods.name: Pizza, burgers, and fast food
foods.fat: High
foods.line: A flare day is a bad day for a drive-through.

foods.name: Nuts, nut butter, and avocado
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Leave peanut butter, almonds, and avocado for a steadier day, and then only in small amounts if your dietitian agrees.
foods.note: These are not junk. They are just too much fat for a flare.

foods.name: Very spicy food
foods.line: Hot sauce, hot wings, and heavy spice blends. They are a common pain trigger on a sore day.

foods.name: Tuna packed in oil
foods.fat: High
foods.line: The water-packed can is on the eat list. The oil-packed can is not.

foods.name: Pastry and chips
foods.fat: High
foods.line: Chips, pie, cookies, and buttery crackers.
foods.note: Plain saltines and plain rice cakes are the cracker exception.

foods.name: A large meal
foods.line: Even plain food hurts more when the portion is huge. Small, then stop, then wait.
foods.note: Mayo Clinic and the National Pancreas Foundation both point to smaller meals.

foods.name: Strong coffee and energy drinks
foods.line: NIDDK says to limit caffeine. On a flare day, drink water or broth first.
foods.note: This is not a forever ban written by Harbor. It is a flare-day choice. Ask your clinician what is right on steady weeks.
